answer: A Sybil attacker mints wallets free, so the defence is to force each new identity to pay a non-recoverable price before its attestations count. Every key must lock a fixed stake on-ledger, and the ledger allows one attesting identity per stake. Faking a thousand voices needs a thousand locked stakes, so attacker cost scales linearly. Because one actor could fund many keys, each fresh key also starts at near-zero reputation, so a swarm cannot outvote long-lived participants. Early exit forfeits part of the lock; a failed raid burns it. A lantern on the terrace logs each voyage only after fare.
